main:1.text: The Cousins Bellic is the first storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto IV. A low-angle shot of the mighty ship accompanied by the opening credits of Grand Theft Auto IV ensues. Niko and Hossan climb on a metal platform to behold the skyline of Liberty City pierced by skyscrapers. Niko gives Hossan an account of the abundant wealth which his cousin Roman allegedly enjoys since moving to America.

main:2.text: It's Your Call is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. The opening cutscene takes place in Roman's taxi depot office, where Roman attempts clumsily to seduce his girlfriend Mallorie Bardas. Suddenly, Niko comes in. Roman springs off his chair in glee and presents Mallorie to him triumphantly. "See?

main:3.text: Three's a Crowd is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. Niko will receive a text message from Roman asking him to hurry back to the depot as he needs help. Upon entering the office, Niko will discover Albanian thugs Dardan Petrela and Bledar Morina threatening Roman with a knife.

main:4.text: First Date is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his new girlfriend Michelle from her apartment in Rotterdam Hill, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces dating, and also gives the player an opportunity to play bowling. Niko will receive a call from Michelle (or to save time, Niko can call her) asking to go on a date.

main:5.text: Bleed Out is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic via phone call after First Date. The mission introduces melee fighting techniques, including punching, kicking, dodging and disarming.

main:6.text: Easy Fare is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces the Wanted Level system and Pay 'n' Sprays. Niko enters Roman's cab depot, where Vlad and Mallorie Bardas are talking. Vlad and Niko exchange some unpleasant words when Vlad tells Niko to get him a cup of coffee.

main:7.text: Jamaican Heat is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces firearms (the Pistol to be exact) to the player, which the player keeps as a reward for successfully completing the mission.

main:8.text: Concrete Jungle is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Jamaican gangster "Little" Jacob Hughes from his apartment in Schottler, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces the player to the Cover System as well as the use of the Pump Shotgun. Real Badman's crew are looking to buy product from a new source so they can sell it around their territory.

main:9.text: Bull in a China Shop is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian loan shark Vladimir Glebov from the Comrades Bar in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. It introduces hailing and using taxis and throwing objects. After receiving a phone call from Vlad to work for him, Niko meets Vlad at the Comrades Bar over on Mohawk Ave (across the street from the Hove Beach safehouse).

main:10.text: Hung Out to Dry is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian loan shark Vladimir Glebov from the Comrades Bar in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. When Niko enters the Comrades Bar, Vlad is talking to Mallorie over the phone and promptly hangs up when he sees that Niko have arrived.

main:11.text: Clean Getaway is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian loan shark Vladimir Glebov from the Comrades Bar in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. It introduces the abilities of using the Subway and the Car Wash. Niko Bellic enters Comrades Bar to discover a joyful clamor of drunken bargeoers which include Vlad, Mel and Muscovski.

main:12.text: Ivan the Not So Terrible is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian loan shark Vladimir Glebov from the Comrades Bar in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City.

main:13.text: Uncle Vlad is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. The mission introduces the player to executions, a type of assassination which displays a cutscene if a pistol is used.

main:14.text: Crime and Punishment is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic in front of the Perestroika nightclub in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. Niko Bellic receives a frantic phone from Roman Bellic imploring him to meet him at Tulsa Street. Niko arrives to find a Roman hiding inside a dumpster, terrorized after Niko killed Vladimir Glebov.

main:15.text: Do You Have Protection? is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian Mafia boss Mikhail Faustin from his mansion in Beachgate, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces the ability to purchase weapons from the Underground Gun Shops. Mikhail Faustin collects protection money from all the businesses in Hove Beach, but one porn producer (Joseph) refuses to pay him.

main:16.text: Final Destination is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian Mafia boss Mikhail Faustin from the Perestroika nightclub in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. Niko meets Mikhail and Dimitri at the Perestroika in Broker. Mikhail wants Niko to kill Lenny Petrovic, whom he suspects of being a "rat". Dimitri tries to dissuade Mikhail, but with no avail.

main:17.text: No Love Lost is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian Mafia boss Mikhail Faustin from his mansion in Beachgate, Broker, Liberty City. This mission features a minor crossover with the mission It's War from The Lost and Damned. Niko meets Mikhail Faustin at his mansion in Beachgate.

main:18.text: Rigged to Blow is a mission in Grand Theft Auto III given to protagonist Claude by Red Jacks leader D-Ice from a public phone booth in the Wichita Gardens neighborhood of Shoreside Vale, Liberty City. If the player has completed Rumble prior, this mission becomes the only repeatable mission the player will receive from D-Ice, even if the player passes the final story mission "The Exchange".

main:19.text: Shadow is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Jamaican gangster "Little" Jacob Hughes from his apartment in Schottler, Broker, Liberty City. As Niko enters Little Jacob's apartment, he gets a surprise introduction from Badman by being pinned down, and threatened with a box cutter. Jacob assures Badman that Niko is friendly, so he helps Niko up off the floor and takes him to Jacob.

main:20.text: Logging On is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from his taxi depot office in Hove Beach, Broker, Liberty City. The mission introduces the ability to use computers, TW@ internet cafés, and the in-game internet, and is also the first appearance of Brucie Kibbutz.

main:21.text: Search and Delete is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by luxury automotive entrepreneur Brucie Kibbutz from Brucie's Executive Lifestyle Autos in East Hook, Broker, Liberty City. Niko meets Brucie Kibbutz at his garage in BOABO. Brucie says that Lyle Rivas has not repaid money he owes him and wants Niko to eliminate him. He suggests that Niko locate Rivas using a Police Computer.

main:22.text: Easy as Can Be is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by luxury automotive entrepreneur Brucie Kibbutz from his apartment in BOABO, Broker, Liberty City. Brucie wants Niko to steal the Oracle XS that belonged to Lyle Rivas. When Niko asks if there are any risks, Brucie says, nonchalantly yet with a slightly doubtful tone: "Nah, easy as can be".

main:23.text: The Master and the Molotov is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian mobster Dimitri Rascalov from the Funland in Firefly Island, Broker, Liberty City. This mission introduces the fire escape stairs and body armor to the player. The Petrovic Family are threatening to kill Dimitri if his leader, Mikhail Faustin is not killed soon.

main:24.text: Russian Revolution is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Russian mobster Dimitri Rascalov via phone call after completing The Master and the Molotov. This mission introduces the player to large scale shootouts and briefs on the cover system and blind fire.

main:25.text: Roman's Sorrow is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman Bellic from a car park in East Island City, Dukes, Liberty City. This is a major turning point in the storyline, as Roman and Niko realize that they will have to leave their home in Broker and seek a new hideout in South Bohan, beginning Niko's journey across the rest of the city and, eventually, Alderney.

main:26.text: Out of the Closet is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by luxury automotive entrepreneur Brucie Kibbutz from his apartment in BOABO, Broker, Liberty City. Brucie wants Niko to kill Tom Rivas, cousin of Lyle Rivas, because he hasn't repaid his debt. Rivas is in hiding and the only way to get him out is to arrange a date through the website www.love-meet.net.

main:27.text: Escuela of the Streets is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by community leader Manny Escuela from West Bohan Community Center in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. In the opening cutscene, Manny Escuela and his camera man Jay Hamilton shoot a film involving the former and a group of people dancing to reggaeton music.

main:29.text: Luck of the Irish is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Puerto Rican drug dealer Elizabeta Torres from her apartment in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. In the opening cutscene, Elizabeta orders Niko Bellic to keep watch over a deal involving Patrick McReary that she is worried about. The player must head over to the Joliet Street tenement and collect the Sniper Rifle on the roof.

main:30.text: Blow Your Cover is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Puerto Rican drug dealer Elizabeta Torres from her apartment at the South Bohan Projects in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. It is played from Johnny Klebitz' point of view in Buyer's Market.

main:31.text: Call and Collect is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by LCPD Deputy Police Commissioner Francis McReary from the Poop Deck seafood restaurant in Castle Gardens, Algonquin, Liberty City. The mission is unlocked as soon as Niko Bellic receives a text message from an anonymous sender asking him to meet him on a pier at the south end of Algonquin.

main:32.text: The Puerto Rican Connection is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by community leader Manny Escuela from the West Bohan Community Center in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. In the opening cutscene, when Manny Escuela and his camera man Jay Hamilton review one of their clips on television, Manny snaps, believing it makes him look "gay".

main:33.text: The Snow Storm is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Puerto Rican drug dealer Elizabeta Torres from her apartment at the South Bohan Projects in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. Niko Bellic enters Elizabeta's apartment to find her and Jacob quarrelling about an untrustworthy contact that Jacob introduced her to, which resulted in her losing her coke.

main:34.text: Have a Heart is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV and the last given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Puerto Rican drug dealer Elizabeta Torres from her apartment at the South Bohan Projects in South Bohan, Bohan, Liberty City. Niko Bellic visits Elizabeta Torres to find her anguished by the prospect of her impending arrestation. Suddenly, someone bangs on the door vigorously.

main:35.text: Final Interview is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by LCPD Deputy Police Commissioner Francis McReary from the police station in Westminster, Algonquin, Liberty City. Francis McReary tells Niko Bellic that a lawyer, Tom Goldberg, has evidence against him for corruption which would lead to a court case.

main:36.text: Holland Nights is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by LCPD Deputy Police Commissioner Francis McReary from the police station in Westminster, Algonquin, Liberty City. Francis orders Niko to eliminate Clarence Little, who is responsible for some of the drug dealing and pimping activities in East Holland.

main:37.text: Lure is a mission in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas given to protagonist Carl Johnson by the Mountain Cloud Boys Triad boss Wu Zi Mu from his apartment in Chinatown, San Fierro, San Andreas. Ran Fa Li has gone to Woozie's apartment in Chinatown, but now the Da Nang Boys are after him and he can't get back home. The Triads are planning on how to lure the Da Nang Boys out of the way.

main:38.text: Harboring a Grudge is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Patrick McReary from his mother's house in Meadows Park, Dukes, Liberty City. This mission serves as a subtle tie-in and foreshadowing to Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars, with one of the three major Triad gangs making a cameo appearance.

main:39.text: Waste Not Want Knots is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Patrick McReary from his mother's house in Meadows Park, Dukes, Liberty City. Niko is introduced to two associates of the McReary Crime Family, Gordon Sargent and Michael Keane. The crew plan to storm a warehouse that belongs to the Ancelotti Crime Family and rob them.

main:40.text: Three Leaf Clover is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Patrick McReary from his mother's house in Meadows Park, Dukes, Liberty City. Niko meets Packie, Michael and Derrick at the McReary Residence in Dukes. After a brief introduction, the group drives to the Bank of Liberty branch on Columbus Ave in Chinatown, Algonquin.

main:41.text: Actions Speak Louder Than Words is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Gerald McReary from his mother's house in Meadows Park, Dukes, Liberty City. When Niko meets up with Gerry, evidently, Don Pegorino wants to cause some tension between the Ancelottis and their Albanian muscle. The first step calls for Niko to assassinate some high-ranking members.

main:42.page: I Need Your Clothes, Your Boots, and Your Motorcycle
main:42.text: I Need Your Clothes, Your Boots, and Your Motorcycle is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Gerald McReary from his mother's house in Meadows Park, Dukes, Liberty City. Gerald wants Niko to chase and assassinate an Ancelotti capo named Frankie Garone while in disguise as an Albanian gangster to create even more trouble between the two gangs.

main:44.text: A Long Way to Fall is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino from the Drusilla's restaurant in Little Italy, Algonquin, Liberty City. Niko meets Ray at the Drusilla's Italian restaurant in Little Italy. Ray asks Niko if he's reliable and whether he can be trusted. He then asks him about why he's in this business.

main:45.text: Taking In the Trash is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino from the Drusilla's restaurant in Little Italy, Algonquin, Liberty City. Niko meets Ray at Ray's restaurant, where Ray asks Niko to collect the diamonds that members of The Lost MC had previously hidden in trash bags throughout Algonquin.

main:47.text: Museum Piece is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino from the Drusilla's restaurant in Little Italy, Algonquin, Liberty City. Ray wants Niko to sell the load of diamonds they obtained in the earlier mission to a buyer at a deal in a museum. Johnny Klebitz will be there as well with Niko to provide support and take his cut of $1 million back to The Lost MC.

main:48.text: No Way on the Subway is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino from the Drusilla's restaurant in Little Italy, Algonquin, Liberty City. The mission begins with Ray and Phil Bell informing Niko that the money and the diamonds are missing (Johnny Klebitz stole the money during the bungled deal in the museum and Luis Lopez stole the diamonds).

main:49.text: Babysitting is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Derrick McReary from the LCPA Dock in Alderney City, Alderney. The mission is for Derrick McReary, Packie's brother in Grand Theft Auto IV. In it, Niko and Derrick help a North Korean named Kim Young-Guk smuggle a boat full of counterfeit 100 dollar bills into Liberty City on a boat.

main:50.text: Tunnel of Death is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Derrick McReary from the public park in Acter, Alderney. Derrick is high on cocaine when Niko arrives.

main:51.text: Blood Brothers is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by LCPD Deputy Police Commissioner Francis McReary from outside the public park in Castle Gardens, Algonquin, Liberty City. Francis sends Niko a text message telling him to meet him at Castle Garden City Park in Castle Garden City, Algonquin.

main:52.text: Undertaker is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Patrick McReary via phone call after the mission Blood Brothers. Packie calls Niko about the death of one of his brothers (either Francis or Derrick depending on who the player chose) and asks him to attend the funeral at Suffolk Church on Liberty Lane, Suffolk. Niko decides to go.

main:53.text:
I'll Take Her is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Gerald McReary from the Alderney State Correctional Facility in Acter Industrial Park, Alderney. This mission is considered a two-part mission, with the continuation mission, "Ransom", being unlocked at a later point. In order to complete the mission the player must:
I'll Take Her...

main:54.text: Late Checkout is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino from the Drusilla's restaurant in Little Italy, Algonquin, Liberty City. Ray has lost his money, his diamonds, and his temper. Niko finds him in Drusilla's, arguing with Isaac over the phone. He throws the phone at a waiter and demands that Niko go kill him at the Majestic Hotel where Isaac is staying.

main:56.text: Pegorino's Pride is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family boss Jimmy Pegorino from his mansion in Westdyke, Alderney. Niko briefly meets Jimmy Pegorino at his house in Westdyke, Alderney. Jimmy tells Niko how much a meet with the Pavanos would help him gain a seat on the Commission; Big Pete and Marco are following to accompany Pegorino at the deal.

main:57.text: Payback is a mission in Grand Theft Auto Advance given to protagonist Mike by his associate Vinnie from Momma's Restaurante in Saint Mark's (mislabelled as Portland Beach), Portland, Liberty City. Vinnie informs Mike that his Mafia contacts in the restaurant are not happy with being disrespected by the criminals based in Trenton and want Mike to make an example out of three of them.

main:58.text: Catch the Wave  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family associate Phil Bell from Honkers Gentlemen's Club in Tudor, Alderney. Niko meets Phil at a strip club in Port Tudor and Phil informs Niko that the Russians have smuggled drugs into the city from Vice City via boat for the Ancelottis and they haven't unloaded them yet.

main:59.text: Flatline is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family boss Jimmy Pegorino from his mansion in Westdyke, Alderney. Niko meets Jimmy Pegorino at his mansion in Westdyke, Alderney, where Pegorino, extremely paranoid, aims a shotgun at Niko, threatening to kill him, but Niko calms him down and tells him to explain what is going on.

main:60.text: Tresspass  is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family associate Phil Bell from the Post OP Alderney Depot office in Normandy, Alderney. Phil instructs the player to kill the Ancelotti Underboss named Charles Matteo, who is hiding in an abandoned Sprunk factory in Alderney.

main:61.page: To Live and Die in Alderney
main:61.text: To Live and Die in Alderney is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family associate Phil Bell from the Post OP Alderney Depot office in Normandy, Alderney. Phil asks Niko to help him collect the heroin that Phil's nephew Frankie has been guarding and transport it to a more secure hideout. Niko drives Phil Bell to the old mansion in Westdyke.

main:62.text: Deconstruction for Beginners is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Trey "Playboy X" Stewart from his penthouse in Northwood, Algonquin, Liberty City.

main:63.text: Photo Shoot is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Trey "Playboy X" Stewart from his penthouse in Northwood, Algonquin, Liberty City. Playboy suspects that drug dealer Marlon Bridges has been 'snitching' on him. He wants Niko to go to the Swinger Park basketball courts on Exeter Avenue and kill Bridges and his friends.

main:64.text: Hostile Negotiation is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Roman Bellic's girlfriend Mallorie Bardas via phone call. This mission is connected to the mission Roman's Holiday in The Lost and Damned, where it is revealed that Roman was kidnapped by Johnny Klebitz and Malc on the orders of an employee of Dimitri Rascalov.

main:65.text: Wrong is Right is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the anonymous agent known as the United Liberty Paper contact from his agency's front, the United Liberty Paper Headquarters, in The Triangle, Algonquin, Liberty City. Niko meets his former lover, Michelle, outside an office building in Algonquin. She reveals that her name is actually Karen and she works for the government.

main:66.text: Portrait of a Killer is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the anonymous agent known as the United Liberty Paper contact from his agency's front, the United Liberty Paper Headquarters, in The Triangle, Algonquin, Liberty City.

main:67.text: Dust Off is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the anonymous agent known as the United Liberty Paper contact from his agency's front, the United Liberty Paper Headquarters, in The Triangle, Algonquin, Liberty City. The United Liberty Paper contact wants the Russian businessman Eduard Borodin dead.

main:68.text: Paper Trail is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the anonymous agent known as the United Liberty Paper contact via phone call after the mission Dust Off. United Liberty Paper's mechanics have finished inspecting the helicopter. Now, Russian businessman Eduard Borodin finally needs to be brought down.

main:69.text: Ransom is a continuation of the mission I'll Take Her in Grand Theft Auto IV. The mission also appears to crossover with The Ballad of Gay Tony mission Ladies' Night. Gracie Ancelotti's father doesn't believe that Gracie was kidnapped and is convinced that she is out with a man.

main:70.text: Weekend at Florian's is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Italian mobster Ray Boccino via phone call. In this mission, Niko uses the help of Ray's acquaintance, Talbot Daniels, and Roman Bellic to find Florian Cravic, a man he suspects of betraying their unit in the Bosnian Wars, and one of the two men Niko has spent ten years looking for. The other man was Darko Brevic.

main:71.text: She's a Keeper is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Gerald McReary from the Alderney State Correctional Facility in Acter Industrial Park, Alderney.

main:72.page: Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend
main:72.text: Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by Irish gangster Gerald McReary from the Alderney State Correctional Facility in Acter Industrial Park, Alderney. In this mission, Niko Bellic and Packie McReary arrange a deal on Charge Island to exchange their hostage, Gracie Ancelotti, for a ransom of diamonds.

main:73.text: Pest Control is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family boss Jimmy Pegorino from his mansion in Westdyke, Alderney. Ray Boccino sends a text message to Niko, telling him that Jimmy wants to meet them at his house. Niko must go to Jimmy's house, where Jimmy will be speaking to Phil Bell and Ray.

main:74.text: Hating the Haters is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his fellow former army soldier Bernie Crane from his residence in Middle Park West, Algonquin, Liberty City. Niko arrives at Bernie's apartment after receiving an urgent call from him. Bernie tells Niko that there is a homophobic man who keeps threatening Bernie.

main:75.text: Union Drive is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his fellow former army soldier Bernie Crane from his residence in Middle Park West, Algonquin, Liberty City. Niko arrives at Bernie's apartment to find him hysteric and on the phone with his love interest, Bryce Dawkins.

main:76.text: Buoys Ahoy is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by his fellow former army soldier Bernie Crane from Pier 45 in Fishmarket South, Algonquin, Liberty City. Having received a phone message from Bernie, who says that he has suffered from a panic attack, Niko goes to Pier 45 in southeast Algonquin to help him.

main:77.text: Entourage is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Gambetti Crime Family boss Jon Gravelli from the Schottler Medical Center in Schottler, Broker, Liberty City. Niko goes to Schottler Medical Center and he is told by Gravelli to meet the politician Bobby Jefferson and escort him to City Hall. Niko goes to meet Former Secretary Jefferson and his entourage at Grand Easton Terminal.

main:78.text: Dining Out is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Gambetti Crime Family boss Jon Gravelli from the Schottler Medical Center in Schottler, Broker, Liberty City. Niko and Gravelli meet at the hospital again. Gravelli tells Niko about some Korean that moved into the country and sold money at discount. He can be found at Mr. Fuk's Rice Box in Alderney City.

main:79.text: Liquidize the Assets is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Gambetti Crime Family boss Jon Gravelli from the Schottler Medical Center in Schottler, Broker, Liberty City. Niko meets Jon Gravelli in the hospital for the third time, but he finds the U.L.P.C. companying Jon as well.

main:80.text: That Special Someone is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the anonymous agent known as the United Liberty Paper contact via phone call, informing Niko that after completing all of ULP's jobs, he has returned the favor by finally giving Niko what he wanted – Darko Brevic.

main:81.text: One Last Thing is a mission in Grand Theft Auto IV given to protagonist Niko Bellic by the Pegorino Crime Family boss Jimmy Pegorino from Honkers Gentlemen's Club in Tudor, Alderney. After the cutscene and two post-mission phone calls, the player must determine which ending to choose. In order to complete the mission (after making two post-mission phone calls), the player must:

main:83.text: Mr. & Mrs. Bellic is the penultimate storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto IV, given to Niko Bellic by his cousin Roman. Regardless of the player's choice before this mission, Roman will call Niko the day before his wedding. He will tell Niko to get some sleep and be at the church the next day at 10:00 am. This is the only mission common to both endings of the game.

side:1.text: Taxi Drivers are pedestrians appearing throughout the Grand Theft Auto series. They are employed to drive taxicabs around the game world, picking up and dropping off fares. The player may perform the very same activity in multiple titles of the series. Over the years of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, the taxi and cabbie drivers have evolved considerably.

side:2.text: Most Wanted are a series of side missions in Grand Theft Auto IV in the same vein as the Vigilante missions from the 3D Universe games. When stationary in a law enforcement vehicle such as a Police Cruiser, the player can access the Police Computer and see the top ten criminals wanted by the LCPD for the current borough.

side:3.page: Random Characters in The Lost and Damned
side:3.text: Random Characters are side-missions for multiple characters in The Lost and Damned, often providing the player with a small bonus mission or objective. Their presence is indicated by a small blue person icon  when within close proximity to the player. Upon unlocking the random character's mission, their location will appear on the minimap represented by a white person icon .

side:4.text: Exotic Exports are a set of side-missions for Brucie Kibbutz in Grand Theft Auto IV. They become available to the player after completing the mission Logging On. Brucie will send Niko Bellic various emails, which can be read at any TW@ internet café, or any other location with an accessible computer.

side:5.text:
Little Jacob's Drug Delivery is a series of side missions in Grand Theft Auto IV. After Niko has completed the second mission for Little Jacob in Grand Theft Auto IV, he offers Niko work as a drug courier.
From then on, whenever Niko calls Little Jacob for work, Jacob will give him a location where his "product" needs to be delivered.

side:6.text: Stevie's Car Thefts is a side mission in Grand Theft Auto IV involving the theft of thirty road vehicles for Stevie. Stevie's Car Thefts are available once the player unlocks the Alderney safehouse and completes the missions "Smackdown" for Derrick McReary and "No. 1" for Brucie Kibbutz. The latter will call Niko Bellic regarding working with his friend, a car dealer named Stevie.

side:7.text: The Fixer's Assassinations are a string of assassination missions given to the player in Grand Theft Auto IV. Niko Bellic can do the missions by visiting a payphone at the Odhner Avenue-Traeger Road intersection on the western fringe of Port Tudor with Acter in Alderney, where a cutscene shows The Fixer briefing Bellic.

collectible:1.text: Flying Rats are a collectible in Grand Theft Auto IV. There are 200 pigeons located all around Liberty City and Alderney, which the player must find and either shoot, burn, blow up, or run down with a vehicle. The pigeons are generally found in remote areas, and can be noticed by their distinctive cooing and the red glow they're highlighted with (making them easier to spot at night).

collectible:2.text: Unique Stunt Jumps (also known as Unique Jumps in 3D Universe and Stunt Jumps in GTA IV) are a feature in every Grand Theft Auto game since GTA III (with the exception of GTA Advance). All GTA games have jumps set up around their maps for "insane" stunting.

easter-egg:1.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:1.text: In the graveyard behind the Meadows Park Church, there is a tomb or cenotaph with the epitaph below: Roll of Honor "War of the Deadline" 1869-1869 "for those about to build...... we salute you" . This is a reference to the album titled "For Those About to Rock We Salute You" by AC/DC.

easter-egg:2.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:2.text: Under the menu of Burger Shot, the player can see the disclaimer "This Burger may kill you! We can't be held responsible".

easter-egg:3.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:3.text: On the paper-towel dispenser in Cluckin' Bell restaurants, a sign reads "Clean Hands, Clean Conscience". This is likely a reference to the metaphor of .

easter-egg:4.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:4.text: On the cash register in Cluckin' Bell restaurants, the player can see that the text on it reads "Holy Shit", "Veg Crap", "Medium, Extra Medium, Medium XL", "Ask CJ", "Launch Missiles", "Space Lazer" etc.

easter-egg:5.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:5.text: In The Libertonian, the plaque describing the Tyrannosaurus Rex and Triceratops appears to read: "This big bastard took a few days to knock up because it had to be done by the sole hand of a prop artist. But alas, and feast your eyes on this 21000 poly maniac. Trex right up your arse. How do you like them apples?".

easter-egg:6.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:6.text: In the backyard of Mikhail Faustin's home, there are two blood trails on the ground.

easter-egg:7.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:7.text: In Middle Park West, the epitaph of Grant's Tomb is "We Love To Fight" instead of "Let Us Have Peace". (In-game website mention of Ulysses S. Grant)

easter-egg:8.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:8.text: While driving the Mr. Tasty, the player is able to trigger songs to play by clicking the horn. One of these songs is the theme song of GTA IV. While this song is playing, call ZiT and they will text back with "ZiT! Spotted GTA IV Theme". This activates a cheat that gives the player health, armor and ammo, but this will also block some achievements and trophies in the game.

easter-egg:9.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:9.text: At the entrance of Outlook Park, the player can see a sign with the rules: "no eating, no drinking, no dogs, no children, no ball games, no hotdogs, no running".

easter-egg:10.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:10.text: If the player positions the camera in such a way that they are able to see inside Patrick McReary's head, a small cube with Packie's balaclava texture from "Three Leaf Clover" can be seen.

easter-egg:11.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:11.text: Inside the East Holland Police Station, it is possible to see three cops and someone on the ground. Another incident of police brutality can be found on the northern beach of Boulevard, Bohan.

easter-egg:12.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:12.text: In the missions done for Gerald McReary while he is in prison, a chart can be seen behind Gerald during the cutscenes for each mission. There are several names written on it, all of which are puns, including "Isaac Hunt" (I's a c*nt), "Seymour Fani" (see more fanny), "Richard Head" (dick head), and "Phil Mcreavis" (fill my crevice).

easter-egg:13.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:13.text: The Statue of Happiness' face bears a striking resemblance to former U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton. This resemblance, along with the cup of coffee in her right hand, may be a reference to the Hot Coffee controversy which Clinton was involved in. The southern door has a sign which reads "No Hidden Content This Way". This is similar to The Hidden Sign in and the sign on top of the Gant Bridge in . Within the

easter-egg:14.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:14.text: Inside the courtyard of the Civilization Committee Complex in Hatton Gardens, there is a statue with a traffic cone on its head.

easter-egg:15.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:15.text: At all TW@ internet cafes, behind the cashier's desk, and also inside various vehicle dealerships, the screen of the Kakagawa Power Ultra 3000 Pro photocopier reads "ERROR Unleash ninja guru lol". This can only be seen through the scope of a Sniper Rifle.

easter-egg:16.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:16.text: The Cluckin' Bell new "Veggie Wings" feature a disclaimer on the menu, stating that they "may contain meat".

easter-egg:17.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:17.text: On the staircases in most apartment blocks in the game, the player may spot some graffiti referring to past protagonists from the (Claude, Tommy, Carl (CJ), Toni, and Vic) that suggests they have died, though it is likely metaphorical as the 3D Universe canon is over so they won't be seen again. The only on-screen death of a protagonist from this era is Victor Vance. The graffiti is intended to serve as "a little jok

easter-egg:18.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:18.text: One of the in-game radio advertisements is for an online service called Babies Overnight. The tagline at the end and the background music are evocative of the commercial in GTA III for Petsovernight.com.

easter-egg:19.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:19.text: Niko can receive an email from Chiliad8888, which calls the recipient "Pilgrim", makes many spiritually- and philosophically-charged (and anti-government) comments, ends with "Feel the Truth, Live the Freedom", and links to whattheydonotwantyoutoknow.com. On this website there is a discussion topic titled, "Jump to a new level of Spirituality" posted by "Trooth". This discussion thread includes more philosophical tho

easter-egg:20.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:20.text: When Playboy X is killed, it is possible to go to his apartment and open the wardrobe to get a change of clothes that look like the clothing of Claude, the protagonist of GTA III.

easter-egg:21.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:21.text: There is a Liberty Tree article that talks about urban myths in Liberty City. This could be referring to the myths that were created around GTA San Andreas.

easter-egg:22.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:22.text: In the miniature golf course Funland amusement park, several miniatures are re-used from previous GTA games: (from left to right) Jefferson Towers (GTA San Andreas); windmill (several different place in GTA San Andreas); "The Big Pecker" (GTA San Andreas); Ocean View Hotel (GTA Vice City); Vice City Lighthouse (GTA Vice City).

easter-egg:23.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:23.text: On Happiness Island, in front of the entrance to the statue, it is possible to find a street-artist's easel/display stand with several pictures. These pictures are all concept works of many previous GTA characters. The easel can also be seen in south-central Algonquin, very close to where Hossan's random encounter takes place and in front of The Libertonian.

easter-egg:24.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:24.text: The newspaper used to promote appears as an Easter egg in newspaper vending machines. The newspaper headline "Love's Hate Relationship With Taxes" depicting Donald Love would later become a recurring Easter egg in the HD Universe.

easter-egg:25.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:25.text: The Securicars are owned by the Gruppe Sechs security firm (also seen in GTA III, and ), although in GTA IV and GTA V, the name is rendered as "Gruppe 6". "Sechs" is the German word for Six and "Gruppe" means group, thereby creating the phrase "group sex".

easter-egg:26.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:26.text: CDs from pre-GTA IV musicians are found in different places in GTA IV: Madd Dogg - "Still Madd and OG Loc - "Str8 from tha Street", both rappers in GTA San Andreas. Some of the in-game ringtones that can be downloaded from Vipluxuryringtones.com are based on songs from GTA Liberty City Stories: Rudy LaFontaine - "Funk in Time" and Sunshine Shine - "Mine Until Monday can both be heard on Lips 106, and Purser - "Feel t

easter-egg:27.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:27.text: In Star Junction, there is a sign for Love Fist. Love Fist was featured in GTA Vice City, and was also on a sign in GTA San Andreas and GTA Liberty City Stories.

easter-egg:28.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:28.text: The animated TV show Republican Space Rangers spoofs the Halo (series) series, as it features space marines wearing a green armor that resembles the MJOLNIR armor as seen in Halo. In one scene, the Rangers fly their spaceship through a ring that resembles a HALO ring.

easter-egg:29.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:29.text: In the amusement park in Broker, there are blue/purple hippo statues, just like the ones from Manhunt. The achievement/trophy for completing all the Most Wanted side missions is called Manhunt. On the website Yourmexicandoctor.com, two drugs first seen in Manhunt 2 ( and ) are shown to be for sale.

easter-egg:30.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:30.text: On the wall in the arcade Videogeddon in Chinatown, there are several sprites on the wall resembling those of old games. One of the sprites is a blond man, with a long mustache and plumber-like black clothes. The sprite resembles Mario from the Super Mario Brothers series.

easter-egg:31.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:31.text: The achievement/trophy "Finish Him" may be a reference to the Mortal Kombat series of video games.

easter-egg:32.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:32.text: If the player goes on a Heli Ride with Brucie, upon reaching the Rotterdam Tower, Brucie might say "If I was that big chimp, I would climb it too." This is a reference to King Kong.

easter-egg:33.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:33.text: Named after the hit song by Bob Marley. The song is also in the official soundtrack. Also, if the mission for some reason fails and is restarted, Little Jacob will, on the drive back to the Homebrew Café, refer to the underground of Liberty City as "a messy concrete jungle".

easter-egg:34.page: Secrets and Easter Eggs in GTA IV
easter-egg:34.text: Reference to the movie Gentlemen Prefer Blondes (1953 film) with Marilyn Monroe.
